summary: A humorous parody of the Christmas carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, listing the endless gripes of computer support work, such as broken databases and failing hardware. It is an informational memo, with no technical content.

plainLanguage.summary: This informational memo parodies “The Twelve Days of Christmas” with a growing list of technology problems. Each verse repeats earlier troubles and adds another computer-support complaint.

subtitle: A Christmas-carol parody that adds one computer-support problem each day.

tldr.problem: The song's narrator faces an accumulating list of computer and network support problems.
tldr.mechanism: The memo parodies “The Twelve Days of Christmas,” repeating earlier troubles while adding new technology mishaps in each verse.
tldr.outcome: The final verse combines the accumulated database, hardware, software, and support problems into a comic refrain.

today: RFC 1882 is Informational and presents a technology-support parody in the form of a Christmas carol. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: A Technology-Themed Carol
sections.content: The memo adapts the repeated structure of “The Twelve Days of Christmas” to computer support. The first verse begins with a database that has a broken B-tree, and later verses repeat that problem while adding others.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC uses the carol's repeating verses to build a list of technology troubles. The broken database returns throughout the song.

sections.title: Problems Added in Each Verse
sections.content:
The accumulating complaints include transceiver failures, support calls, SCSI contacts, games on the production network, license failures, dialing modems, SNMP alerts, failing boards, and virtual-pipe connections. The verses also include frustrated remarks about users, hardware, and support work.

By the twelfth day, all the listed problems recur in one final verse.
sections.plainLanguage: Each verse adds another operational problem, from network hardware failures to software licenses and support calls. The final verse repeats them all.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1882 is an Informational poem and does not specify an Internet standard. Its verses repeat earlier complaints and add new technology problems.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a humorous informational memo, not a technical specification.
